lead_recommendation: s1 — Halcyon cut Tern 3 input pricing by 60% and published the per-request latency numbers behind it, which changes the buy-vs-build math for anyone running retrieval at scale.

noise_check.what_evidence_supports: Orvex's own table shows Marlin-27B ahead on LedgerBench-Code by 1.4 points at pass@1 with 8 samples; the Tern 3 model card reports pass@1 with 1 sample. The comparison is not like for like.

research_gaps: Halcyon has not published Tern 3 output-token latency at the 128K context tier.

stories.headline: Halcyon cuts Tern 3 input pricing by 60% and publishes latency data
stories.one_line: Tern 3 input tokens drop from $2.50 to $1.00 per million; a new latency page shows p50 and p99 by context tier.
stories.what_happened: Halcyon Labs announced on September 8 that Tern 3 input pricing falls from $2.50 to $1.00 per million tokens effective immediately, with output pricing unchanged at $10.00 per million. The same post introduced a public latency page reporting p50 and p99 time-to-first-token by context tier.
stories.what_is_new: The price cut is the first since Tern 3 launched in May 2026. The latency page is new; Halcyon previously published no latency figures.
stories.why_it_matters: At $1.00 per million input tokens, long-context retrieval workloads that were cheaper to serve on open-weight models become cheaper on Tern 3 for teams without their own GPUs, according to Halcyon's own cost calculator.
stories.unknowns: Halcyon did not say whether the cut applies to batch pricing. No figures for the 128K tier were published.

facts.claim: Tern 3 input pricing falls from $2.50 to $1.00 per million tokens
Output pricing is unchanged at $10.00 per million tokens
p50 time-to-first-token at the 32K context tier is 410 ms; p99 is 1.9 s
Tern 3 launched in May 2026
The cut makes Tern 3 cheaper than self-hosted Marlin-27B for retrieval workloads under 40M tokens per day

quotes.text: We are pricing input tokens at what they cost us to serve plus a margin we can defend, and publishing the latency numbers so nobody has to take our word for it.
quotes.speaker: Priya Raman

sources.title: Halcyon slashes Tern 3 prices as open-weight rivals close in

stories.headline: Orvex releases Marlin-27B under Apache 2.0
stories.one_line: A 27B-parameter open-weight model with a 256K context window and a permissive licence.
stories.what_happened: Orvex published Marlin-27B weights on September 4 under the Apache 2.0 licence, with a 256K token context window and a technical report.
stories.what_is_new: Orvex's previous release, Marlin-12B, used a custom licence that barred commercial use above 10 million monthly active users. Marlin-27B has no such clause.
stories.why_it_matters: Teams that rejected Marlin-12B on licence grounds can now deploy the family commercially without a negotiation.
stories.unknowns: The technical report does not disclose training data composition beyond 'web, code, and licensed text'.

facts.claim: Marlin-27B is released under Apache 2.0
Context window is 256K tokens
Marlin-27B scores 71.2 on LedgerBench-Code at pass@1 with 8 samples
Marlin-12B's licence barred commercial use above 10 million monthly active users

stories.headline: Nordic Digital Authority fines Brightline Recruit for undisclosed AI screening
stories.one_line: A €4.2 million fine for using an AI model to reject applicants without telling them.
stories.what_happened: The Nordic Digital Authority fined Brightline Recruit €4.2 million on September 5 for screening 38,000 job applications with an AI model between January and June 2026 without disclosing it to applicants, in breach of the Authority's automated-decision rules.
stories.what_is_new: This is the Authority's first fine under its 2025 automated-decision rules.
stories.why_it_matters: Any company using models to filter people at scale in the Authority's jurisdiction now has a concrete enforcement precedent and a price tag.
stories.unknowns: Brightline has said it will appeal; the timeline is unknown.

facts.claim: The fine is €4.2 million
38,000 applications were screened between January and June 2026
Brightline will appeal

quotes.text: Automated rejection without disclosure is exactly the harm the rules were written to prevent.
quotes.speaker: Ingrid Solberg
quotes.role: Nordic Digital Authority director of enforcement

stories.headline: Cinder Compute opens a 40,000-accelerator cluster in Alberta
stories.one_line: Rentable capacity priced at $1.85 per accelerator-hour on one-year commitments.
stories.what_happened: Cinder Compute announced on September 9 that its Alberta site is live with 40,000 accelerators, priced at $1.85 per accelerator-hour on one-year commitments and $2.60 on demand.
stories.what_is_new: Cinder's previous largest site had 12,000 accelerators.
stories.why_it_matters: The on-demand price undercuts the three largest cloud providers' list prices for comparable hardware, per Cinder's comparison table, which is a vendor claim.
stories.unknowns: Cinder did not say how much of the capacity is already reserved.

facts.claim: 40,000 accelerators at the Alberta site
$1.85 per accelerator-hour on one-year commitments; $2.60 on demand
The on-demand price undercuts the three largest cloud providers

stories.headline: Paper: retrieval order changes long-context answers more than model size
stories.one_line: A controlled study across four models finds document order shifts accuracy by up to 18 points.
stories.what_happened: Researchers at Aldermoor University posted a preprint on September 3 testing four models on the HaystackQA-2 benchmark with retrieved documents in six orderings. Accuracy varied by up to 18 points depending on order, more than the gap between the smallest and largest model tested.
stories.what_is_new: Prior work showed position effects on single models; this study compares the effect size against model scale directly.
stories.why_it_matters: For retrieval pipelines, the ordering step is worth more engineering than model selection, per the study.
stories.unknowns: The study covers models up to 70B parameters; frontier hosted models were not tested.

facts.claim: Accuracy varied by up to 18 points across six orderings
Four models up to 70B parameters were tested on HaystackQA-2

sources.title: Order Matters More Than Scale: Retrieval Ordering Effects in Long-Context QA

stories.headline: Vantage Systems ships agent audit logs to all enterprise tenants
stories.one_line: Every tool call an agent makes is now recorded with inputs, outputs, and the approving policy.
stories.what_happened: Vantage Systems enabled agent audit logs for all enterprise tenants on September 7. Each record captures the tool called, its inputs and outputs, the policy that allowed it, and a 90-day retention window.
stories.what_is_new: Audit logs were previously a paid add-on limited to 30 days of retention.
stories.why_it_matters: Compliance teams that blocked agent deployments for lack of an audit trail lose that objection.
stories.unknowns: Export formats beyond CSV were not announced.

facts.claim: Audit logs are enabled for all enterprise tenants with 90-day retention
Logs were previously a paid add-on with 30-day retention

stories.headline: Talk: how Fennel Health evaluated a triage model before deployment
stories.one_line: A 40-minute conference talk on the evaluation protocol, with the slides published.
stories.what_happened: Fennel Health's head of clinical AI gave a talk on September 6 describing the 14-month evaluation the company ran before deploying a triage model, including a 2,000-case blinded comparison against nurses.
stories.what_is_new: The full protocol and slides are public.
stories.why_it_matters: It is a rare worked example of a pre-deployment evaluation in a regulated setting.
stories.unknowns: The underlying case data is not public.

facts.claim: The evaluation ran 14 months and included a 2,000-case blinded comparison

sources.title: Evaluating a triage model before deployment (slides)
